content:
The test image shows a longitudinally split tomato stem with brown/tan discoloration of the internal vascular tissue and wilted dead leaves in the background. This is a vascular wilt pattern. Top candidates: Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Bacterial_Wilt, Verticillium_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt.

Now viewing one reference from each of the 4 top candidates:

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Longitudinally cut tomato stem showing prominent brown/tan discoloration of internal vascular bundles. Plant is collapsed on black plastic mulch with dead leaves around it. No mycelium, no surface lesions — purely internal vascular browning.
- **Bacterial_Wilt ref (5606063)**: Cross-section of tomato stem with the same brown vascular discoloration pattern, doing the bacterial ooze streaming test. Bugwood IDs 5606057 (test) and 5606063 (reference) are adjacent, strongly indicating same disease.
- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt ref**: Shows leaf yellowing/browning — doesn't match the stem vascular cut pattern.
- **Verticillium_Wilt ref**: Shows external leaf wilting — doesn't match.
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt ref**: Shows bacterial ooze streaming test (green stem, similar to Bacterial_Wilt) — possible, but the test image's brown vascular streaking and the adjacent Bugwood ID point more directly to Bacterial_Wilt.

The longitudinally cut stem with brown vascular tissue is the hallmark of Bacterial_Wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum). The reference image from the same Bugwood sequence confirms this.
